detail.longDescription: SrcWranglr my open-source, Rust-powered C/C++ source-code exploration and security analysis toolkit. I had originally developed this in Python as a prototype for a couple years… That’s until you Rustaceans got in my damn year… If you ever used SourceTrail or Understand, this is my idea of how it should have been done. It helps visualize complex codebases C/C++ it combines interactive call graphs, cross-references, semantic code search, reachability analysis, and inter-procedural value tracing. Security-focused features include vulnerability discovery, attack-surface analysis, automated fuzz harness generation, and integration with external static analyzers. My favorite feature is the ability to generate semgrep rules for the specific code base. Powered by tree-sitter, SrcWranglr can analyze codebases without requiring a successful build or compilation database. Using this tool and my AAVR (Agentic Augmented Vuln Research) methodology I found several vulnerabilities in projects I won’t name as I just disclose to maintainers, in just a couple of hours. https://github.com/jdefrancesco/SrcWranglr
